_comment: Development port takeover, made a SAFETY feature. Feature 129, TAKEOVER-DEC-01/02/03.
`tina4 serve` reclaims a busy port so a restart does not fail with 'address
already in use'. Before this fixture BOTH takeover paths -- the CLI
(killProcessOnPort) and the runtime bind-failure fallback
(_kill_port/freePort/free_port/killPort) -- SIGTERM'd WHATEVER held the port,
with NO check that the victim was a Tina4 dev server (TAKEOVER-NO-IDENTITY). A
foreign holder (another developer's server, a database, a stray http.server)
was killed. The runtime path was the weaker, UNGUARDED twin: no container
guard, no PID-safety filter, no identity check (TAKEOVER-UNGUARDED-RUNTIME).
There was no way to disable it (TAKEOVER-NO-OPTOUT) and it was not gated to dev
(TAKEOVER-NOT-DEV-GATED). See
tina4-documentation/plan/v3/features/129-port-takeover.md and
tina4-documentation/plan/v3/OWNER-DECISIONS.md (Batch 5, TAKEOVER-DEC-01/02/03).
The fix, in all four, is ONE shared takeover helper both paths call
(tina4_python.core.port_takeover / Tina4\PortTakeover / Tina4::PortTakeover /
@tina4/core portTakeover), so the runtime path can never again be a weaker
twin (TAKEOVER-DEC-02):
1. IDENTITY (TAKEOVER-DEC-01): a Tina4 dev server writes a per-port PID file
(data/.tina4-serve-<port>.pid) when it binds and removes it on clean exit.
Takeover signals a holder ONLY when its PID matches that file; a holder
with no matching Tina4 PID file is REFUSED, never killed, with a clear
'port N is held by a non-Tina4 process' message.
2. DEV GATE + OPT-OUT (TAKEOVER-DEC-03): takeover runs ONLY in dev
(TINA4_DEBUG truthy) and ONLY when not opted out (TINA4_NO_TAKEOVER env /
`tina4 serve --no-kill`, which sets the env for the whole process). A
production bind never kills a port holder.
3. The existing PID safety filter (selectable_pids) and container guard stay,
unchanged, on top -- foreign PIDs are still SELECTED by the filter; the
identity check is a SEPARATE, later gate, so the existing selectable_pids
lock-in tests keep passing.
The runtime bind-failure path RAISES on a refused foreign holder, so a bind
onto a foreign-held port fails loudly instead of killing an innocent process.
Refusing is always safe (the developer frees the port by hand); over-killing
was the bug. tina4: identity is a PID+port match against a file Tina4 wrote; the
only false match is PID reuse after an uncleaned crash on the SAME port -- a
tiny window whose failure mode is a refusal, never a wrong kill.
Every case runs with REAL PROCESSES on REAL PORTS, NO MOCKS: each framework
starts a real child that binds a real port (a Tina4 child records its identity
through the REAL framework write_pidfile) and asserts the outcome BY PID -- a
foreign holder is still alive afterwards; a Tina4 holder is gone. The runtime
case drives the real runtime entrypoint (Python _kill_port, PHP Server::freePort
via reflection, Ruby WebServer#free_port, Node killPort).
Mutation-proved (macOS, all four): removing the identity filter in the shared
helper's take_over_port (kill every selectable holder, not just
PID-file-confirmed ones) turns the foreign-holder-spared case AND the
runtime-path-spares-foreign case RED (the foreign child is SIGTERM'd). Restoring
it returns to green.
Each invariant names a REAL suite file per framework and a list of case names;
the four suites carry the SAME case names in each language's own idiom, which
scripts/audit-contract-fixtures.py normalises and matches.

invariants.rule: Port takeover signals a holder ONLY when the holder's PID matches the per-port PID file a Tina4 dev server wrote (data/.tina4-serve-<port>.pid). A holder with no matching Tina4 PID file is REFUSED with a clear 'port N is held by a non-Tina4 process' message and NOT killed. A confirmed Tina4 holder is reclaimed (SIGTERM). Both the CLI path and the runtime bind-failure fallback route through the ONE shared helper, so the runtime path enforces the SAME identity gate (TAKEOVER-DEC-02) and RAISES on a refused foreign holder instead of killing it.
invariants.why: Both takeover paths killed whatever held the port with no Tina4-identity check, so a foreign dev server / database / stray listener was SIGTERM'd on `tina4 serve` (TAKEOVER-NO-IDENTITY), and the runtime path did it with none of the CLI's guards (TAKEOVER-UNGUARDED-RUNTIME). Identifying the victim via a PID file the dev server wrote makes takeover reclaim ONLY a real Tina4 instance. Mutation-proved: dropping the identity filter makes the foreign-holder-spared and runtime-path-spares-foreign cases go RED (the foreign process is killed).
cases: a foreign holder is not killed and takeover refuses
a tina4 dev server holder is reclaimed
the runtime path also spares a foreign holder

invariants.rule: Takeover is gated to dev mode and is opt-out. With takeover opted out (TINA4_NO_TAKEOVER truthy, set by `tina4 serve --no-kill`) it refuses to kill even a confirmed Tina4 holder. Outside dev mode (TINA4_DEBUG not truthy) it refuses to kill any holder -- a production bind never takes over a port. In both cases the holder is left running.
invariants.why: There was no way to disable takeover (TAKEOVER-NO-OPTOUT) and it ran under a production bind too (TAKEOVER-NOT-DEV-GATED) -- killing a port holder in production is surprising. An opt-out env/flag and a dev gate make takeover a dev-only convenience. The gate and opt-out are resolved once and passed into the ONE shared helper, so the CLI and runtime paths honour them identically.
cases: opt out refuses to kill the holder
production mode refuses to kill the holder
